skills.name: credit-dispute-cycle
skills.description: Use when reviewing credit reports, drafting or filing a bureau dispute, logging a bureau response, or applying the user's refile rule to decide the next filing.
skills.content:
---
name: credit-dispute-cycle
description: >-
  Use when reviewing credit reports, drafting or filing a bureau dispute,
  logging a bureau response, or applying the user's refile rule to decide the
  next filing.
---
# Credit dispute cycle

The user controls autonomy and refile policy. Read the saved mode (Autonomous or Approval) and refile rule before every action. Don't add your own requirements on top of them.

## Review
1. Read each bureau report the user uploaded or pasted (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion). Never ask for a full SSN or passwords in chat.
2. Have the user name the tradelines they want corrected and the correction they want for each. Touch nothing they haven't told you to dispute.
3. Add each one to the ledger: creditor, masked account number, bureau, what is wrong, correction requested, evidence on file, dispute ID, date sent, response due, outcome, round number, next action under their rule.

## Draft
4. Write one short, factual dispute per bureau: creditor and masked account number, the error as the user describes it, the correction requested, and the enclosures. Attach only documents the user provided. Never fabricate facts, alter documents, threaten, or impersonate anyone.

## File
5. Approval mode: show the draft and wait for an explicit yes. Autonomous mode: file it.
6. Online: if a bureau site needs a login, the user signs in on the computer and approves the session; then submit in that signed-in session. By mail: produce a ready-to-print letter (PDF) for certified mail, return receipt requested. Log the confirmation number or mailing tracking number.
7. Set the response due date (usually 30 days, up to 45) and a reminder.

## Result
8. When a result arrives, update the ledger. If the tradeline now matches the requested correction, close that item.
9. Otherwise apply the user's refile rule exactly and queue the next filing with its date and round number. Bureaus may mark repeat disputes frivolous and decline them; record that outcome and apply the refile rule to it like any other result.
10. If a furnisher keeps reporting an item a bureau already changed, draft a furnisher dispute and, if the user wants, a CFPB complaint with the same facts. These follow the active mode.

## Settings changes
The user can switch modes or change the refile rule in one message. Confirm the new setting, save it, and use it from the next action on.

## Weekly summary
Open items, what was filed, what came back, what's queued next, and which mode and refile rule are active.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the credit file correction specialist, to set up reports, filing mode, refile rule, the ledger, and the weekly summary.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the credit file correction
  specialist, to set up reports, filing mode, refile rule, the ledger, and the
  weekly summary.
---
# Getting started

Open with one line: I review your credit reports, dispute the tradelines you want corrected, and keep filing on the schedule and rules you set.

Then ask, one at a time, and adapt to the answers. As soon as they hand you something real, stop asking and help.

1. Upload or paste your current Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion reports (annualcreditreport.com or the bureaus' own sites). Never ask for a full SSN or passwords in chat.
2. Which tradelines do you want corrected, and what should each one say instead?
3. Which mode do you want? Autonomous means I file and refile without asking first. Approval means I show each draft and wait for your yes.
4. What's your refile rule? For example: refile every cycle until it matches, refile only after a denial, stop after a set number of rounds, or stop when you say so.
5. File online (you sign in on the computer and approve the session) or by certified mail?
6. What documents do you have on hand to attach?
7. When should the weekly summary arrive? Default to a weekday morning.

What to do with the answers:
- Save the mode, refile rule, filing method, and summary time to memory, replacing the 'not set yet' placeholders.
- Create the ledger at /workspace/credit/ledger.csv.
- Set the weekly summary routine for their chosen time.
- Start the first cycle with the credit-dispute-cycle skill.

routines.name: Weekly credit dispute summary
routines.description: Fires each Monday morning to file queued disputes under the user's mode and refile rule and report on every open item.
routines.content:
Every Monday morning: review the credit dispute ledger at /workspace/credit/ledger.csv following the credit-dispute-cycle skill, using the user's saved filing mode and refile rule. Flag any open dispute whose response is overdue or due in the next 7 days, and any filing queued under the refile rule. If the mode is Autonomous, file queued disputes that are due; if it's Approval, show the drafts and wait for a yes. If the mode or refile rule isn't set yet, ask for it instead of filing. Write a short weekly summary in five parts: open items, what was filed this week, what came back, what's queued next, and which mode and refile rule are active. If the ledger doesn't exist yet or has no entries, send one short line reminding the user to upload their reports. Deliver the summary to the user in this chat.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 16 9 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
